glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.intro: The words {{brand}} uses, and how they relate.
glossary.relation: A service consists of applications. An application runs on systems. {{brand}} reaches systems and applications through platforms.

service.text: What a team offers to others, with an owner and a criticality. It consists of applications.

application.text: Software a service consists of, with a CIA rating. It runs on systems.

system.text: Where applications run: a server, VM, cluster, appliance or cloud service, with its environments. Part of the catalogue.

component.text: A code or data part of an application: a repository, image, library, topic or database.

platform.text: A connection {{brand}} talks to through an API: base URL, credentials, API specifications. Not a catalogue entry.

process.text: A versioned flow of steps that {{brand}} runs. “Procedure” and “runbook” mean the same thing in these docs.

run.text: One execution of a process, with its journal and evidence.

step.text: One node of a process in a run: a call, a check, a manual task or a decision.

decision.text: An approval or selection a person makes while a run waits (My tasks).

monitor.text: A graph of checks that runs on a schedule and reports a status.

check.text: One test inside a monitor or a process step (e.g. HTTP status, a query value).

objective.text: An availability target of a service, measured over time (the scorecard).

document.text: A record with a type and a workflow: change requests, decisions, reviews, firewall changes. In the docs also called a record.

credential.text: Metadata about secrets kept elsewhere (expiry, rotation, owner). It never holds the secret itself; platforms do.

duty.text: A recurring obligation of a service, judged by real runs: done, late or missed.

team.text: A team groups people with roles. The owning teams of an item decide who may see and change it.

module.text: An optional area an administrator can switch off in Settings → Modules.

notYours.title: You do not use this module
notYours.text: Ask an administrator if you need it.
